title: Random forest predicts carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative carriage in ICU patients
summary: Models were built on 1,385 positive and 1,535 negative patients, and a random forest outperformed XGBoost, a decision tree and logistic regression (accuracy 84% vs 72% for logistic regression; AUROC 0.91 vs 0.78). In a 4-month prospective daily prediction across ICU patients accuracy was 85.92% and AUROC 92.02%. It is single-center work.
ai_technology: Random forest compared with XGBoost, decision tree and multivariable logistic regression
organization: Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University

evidence.tested: A 4-month prospective study of daily weekly-risk predictions for all ICU patients.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other hospitals is unknown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML models predicted CR-GNB culture positivity within one week.
